Serous acinar cell.description: Serous acinar cell of airway submucosal glands that secretes antimicrobial proteins including lysozyme, lactoferrin, and SLPI.

Goblet cell.description: Mucous cell of airway epithelium producing gel-forming mucins MUC5AC and MUC5B for mucosal defense.

Club cell.description: Non-ciliated bronchiolar exocrine cell that secretes secretoglobins and metabolizes xenobiotics.

Alveolar type II cell.description: Surfactant-producing alveolar epithelial cell that reduces surface tension and acts as progenitor for alveolar repair.

Alveolar adventitial fibroblast.description: Perivascular fibroblast located in the alveolar interstitium, marked by high expression of COL14A1 and PI16.

Alveolar fibroblast.description: Interstitial fibroblast of the alveolar wall, expressing high levels of MFAP4 and LUM, often confused with adventitial fibroblasts.

Myofibroblast.description: Contractile fibroblast with smooth muscle-like features, expressing ACTA2 and MYH11, commonly arising during repair or fibrosis.

Lipofibroblast.description: Lipid-laden fibroblast residing near alveolar type 2 cells, characterized by PLIN2 and ADIPOQ expression.

Pericyte.description: Perivascular cell wrapping alveolar capillaries, expressing RGS5 and PDGFRB, critical for microvascular stability.

Resident Alveolar Macrophage.description: Tissue-resident alveolar macrophages involved in surfactant clearance and immune surveillance, characterized by lipid metabolism and anti-inflammatory genes.

Proliferating Alveolar Macrophage.description: Proliferating alveolar macrophages marked by cell cycle genes, indicating local self-renewal or expansion during inflammation.

Inflammatory Alveolar Macrophage.description: Activated alveolar macrophages expressing pro-inflammatory cytokines and chemokines, often induced by infection or injury.

Interstitial Macrophage.description: Perivascular interstitial macrophages in the lung parenchyma that support vascular homeostasis and tissue remodeling, distinct from alveolar macrophages by expression of MRC1, CD163, and LYVE1.

Monocyte.description: Blood-derived monocytes that infiltrate the lung, distinguishable from alveolar macrophages by high expression of S100A8, S100A9, and low or absent PPARG and FABP4.

Lipofibroblast.description: Lipid-laden fibroblasts that support alveolar surfactant function and epithelial repair in the distal lung.

Myofibroblast.description: Contractile fibroblasts expressing smooth muscle actin and extracellular matrix components, prominent in fibrotic lung disease.

Alveolar Niche Fibroblast.description: WNT-responsive fibroblasts that maintain alveolar epithelial stem cells and promote epithelial repair.

Matrix Fibroblast.description: Fibroblasts specialized in producing and remodeling the extracellular matrix scaffold of alveolar septa.

Alveolar Type 1 Epithelial Cell.description: Squamous epithelial cells that line the alveolar surface and facilitate gas exchange.

Pericyte.description: Perivascular cells that stabilize capillary walls and regulate microvascular permeability in the lung parenchyma.

Airway Smooth Muscle Cell.description: Contractile cells surrounding conducting airways that regulate bronchomotor tone, sometimes confused with alveolar myofibroblasts.

Naive B cell.description: Mature B cells that have not yet encountered antigen, characterized by co-expression of IgM and IgD.

Memory B cell.description: Antigen-experienced B cells that provide rapid recall responses, often expressing isotype-switched immunoglobulins.

Plasma cell.description: Terminally differentiated B cells specialized in antibody secretion, expressing high levels of immunoglobulin and unfolded protein response genes.

T cell.description: Lymphocytes mediating cellular immunity, distinguishable by expression of CD3 and T cell receptor genes.

NK cell.description: Innate lymphoid cells capable of cytotoxic activity, distinguished by expression of NK cell receptors and lack of CD3.

Mature Goblet Cell.description: Terminally differentiated airway epithelial cell that produces and secretes mucins, particularly MUC5AC, to form the protective mucus layer.

Goblet Cell Precursor.description: Progenitor cell committed to the secretory lineage, expressing Notch signaling components and basal cell markers, capable of differentiating into mature goblet cells.

Club Cell.description: Non-ciliated secretory cell predominantly found in bronchioles, producing secretoglobins and anti-inflammatory proteins, and acting as a progenitor for ciliated cells.

Ciliated Cell.description: Multiciliated epithelial cell with motile cilia responsible for mucociliary clearance in the airways.

Peribronchial fibroblast.description: Fibroblasts surrounding bronchial airways, expressing abundant extracellular matrix components and genes involved in tissue structure, characterized by COL13A1 and FBLN1.

Bronchial myofibroblast.description: Contractile fibroblasts in the bronchial wall, bridging fibroblast and smooth muscle features, expressing alpha-smooth muscle actin (ACTA2) and fibrosis-associated genes.

Airway smooth muscle cell.description: Smooth muscle cells of the airway wall, responsible for bronchoconstriction, commonly confused with myofibroblasts due to overlapping contractile gene expression.

Pericyte.description: Perivascular mural cells wrapping around capillaries and microvessels, often confused with fibroblasts and smooth muscle due to shared mesenchymal markers like RGS5 and PDGFRB.

Bronchiolar brush cell (type 1).description: Chemosensory brush cell subtype enriched in tracheobronchial epithelium and small airways, characterized by high expression of taste receptors and acetylcholine signaling components.

Bronchiolar brush cell (type 2).description: Immune-regulatory brush cell subtype found predominantly in bronchiolar epithelium, expressing cytokines and lipid mediators that influence local immune responses.

Pulmonary neuroendocrine cell.description: Rare chemosensitive pulmonary neuroendocrine cell (PNEC) often confused with brush cells due to shared ASCL1 expression, but distinguished by neuroendocrine markers and peptide secretion.

Pulmonary ionocyte.description: Rare FOXI1-driven airway epithelial cell type specialized for ion transport, frequently misclassified as brush cell due to shared rarity and transcriptional features.

General capillary endothelial cell (gCap.description: General capillary endothelial cells involved in transport, caveolae-mediated transcytosis, and lipoprotein metabolism.

Aerocyte capillary endothelial cell (aCa.description: Specialized capillary endothelial cells (aerocytes) mediating gas exchange and expressing carbonic anhydrase.

Alveolar type I cell.description: Squamous alveolar epithelial cells forming the air-blood barrier, expressing podoplanin and RAGE.

Lymphatic endothelial cell.description: Lymphatic endothelial cells lining lymphatic vessels, expressing Prox1 and Lyve1.

Classical CD1c+ dendritic cells (cDC2).description: Classical type 2 dendritic cells that prime CD4+ T cell responses, highly expressing antigen presentation and costimulatory molecules.

CD1c+CD5+ dendritic cells.description: A subset of CD1c+ dendritic cells characterized by CD5 expression, enriched in immunoregulatory functions and migratory capacity.

CD1c+CD14+ dendritic cells (DC3).description: CD1c+ dendritic cells co-expressing monocyte/macrophage markers, likely monocyte-derived and pro-inflammatory.

Monocytes (CD14+).description: Blood-derived CD14+ monocytes that can infiltrate tissues and differentiate into macrophages or dendritic cells.

Alveolar macrophages.description: Tissue-resident macrophages of the lung alveoli responsible for surfactant catabolism and immune surveillance.

Classical type 1 dendritic cells (cDC1).description: Dendritic cells specialized in cross-presentation to CD8+ T cells, marked by CLEC9A and XCR1.

Plasmacytoid dendritic cells.description: Plasmacytoid DCs specialized in type I interferon production, expressing IL3RA and CLEC4C.

B cells.description: B lymphocytes expressing CD19 and CD20, with surface immunoglobulins and antigen presentation capabilities.

Naive CD4+ T cell.description: Naive CD4+ T cells that have not yet encountered antigen, characterized by high expression of lymphoid homing markers and transcription factors maintaining quiescence.

Tissue-resident memory CD4+ T cell (TRM).description: Tissue-resident memory CD4+ T cells that persist in the lung parenchyma, providing rapid local immune responses upon reinfection.

Regulatory T cell (Treg).description: CD4+ regulatory T cells that suppress immune responses and maintain peripheral tolerance, expressing FOXP3 and other immunomodulatory molecules.

CD8+ T cell.description: Cytotoxic CD8+ T cells, a distinct T cell lineage often confused with CD4+ T cells in annotation due to shared T cell markers, characterized by expression of CD8 and cytotoxic molecules.

NK cell.description: Natural killer cells, innate lymphoid cells that can be confused with T cells, lacking CD3 but expressing NK-specific receptors and cytotoxic mediators.

Naive CD8+ T cell.description: Naive CD8-positive alpha-beta T cells characterized by high expression of lymph node homing receptors, transcription factors maintaining stemness, and low cytotoxic activity.

Effector memory CD8+ T cell.description: Effector memory CD8-positive T cells with rapid effector function, expressing chemokine receptors for tissue homing, cytotoxic granules, and transcription factors TBX21 and EOMES.

Resident memory CD8+ T cell (TRM).description: Resident memory CD8-positive T cells retained in lung tissue, expressing adhesion molecules (CD103, CD49a), tissue-retention signals (CD69, CXCR6), and immediate-early response genes.

Exhausted CD8+ T cell.description: Exhausted CD8-positive T cells with high expression of multiple inhibitory receptors, transcription factors TOX/EOMES, and reduced effector function, often found in chronic infection or tumor microenvironment.

CD4+ T cell.description: CD4-positive alpha-beta T helper cells identified by CD4 expression and lacking CD8, encompassing various subsets including naive, memory, and regulatory T cells.

Natural killer cell.description: Natural killer cells of the innate immune system, characterized by high expression of natural cytotoxicity receptors, killer immunoglobulin-like receptors, and cytolytic molecules, lacking CD3.

Gamma-delta T cell.description: Gamma-delta T cells expressing TRDC and TRGC chains, often with innate-like features, capable of rapid cytokine production and tissue residency.

Classical monocyte (CD14++ FCGR3A-).description: Canonical classical monocytes expressing high CD14 and lacking FCGR3A, with genes involved in phagocytosis and inflammatory response.

Intermediate monocyte (CD14++ FCGR3A+).description: Monocyte subset co-expressing CD14 and FCGR3A, with antigen presentation and interferon signaling signature, bridging classical and non-classical monocytes.

Non-classical monocyte (CD14+ FCGR3A++).description: Patrolling monocytes with high FCGR3A and CX3CR1 expression, involved in endothelial surveillance and antiviral responses.

Monocyte-derived dendritic cell.description: Dendritic cells derived from monocytes in inflamed tissues, expressing CD1c, CLEC10A, and antigen presentation machinery.

Alveolar macrophage.description: Tissue-resident macrophages of the alveolar space characterized by lipid metabolism and surfactant clearance genes, dependent on PPARG.

Secretory Club Cell.description: Differentiated secretory epithelial cells expressing SCGB1A1 and phase I detoxification enzymes, providing bronchiolar protection and surfactant protein production.

Goblet Cell.description: Mucus-producing secretory cells characterized by high expression of mucins MUC5AC and TFF3, often confused with club cells but with distinct morphology.

Ciliated Cell.description: Multiciliated epithelial cells responsible for mucociliary clearance, identifiable by FOXJ1 and cilia-related genes.

Basal Cell.description: Airway epithelial stem/progenitor cells expressing KRT5 and TP63, serving as a reservoir for luminal cell types and often misannotated as club cells.

cDC1.description: Cross-presenting conventional dendritic cells specialized in priming CD8+ T cells, expressing CLEC9A and XCR1.

cDC2.description: Conventional dendritic cells that prime CD4+ T cells, characterized by expression of CD1c and SIRPA.

Alveolar Macrophage.description: Tissue-resident macrophages of the alveolar space, marked by PPARG and MARCO.

Monocyte-derived DC.description: Inflammatory dendritic cells arising from blood monocytes, expressing CD14 and S100A8/A9.

Conventional dendritic cell type 1 (cDC1.description: Professional cross-presenting dendritic cells specialized in priming CD8+ T cells against viral and tumor antigens.

Conventional dendritic cell type 2 (cDC2.description: Main subset of dendritic cells specializing in CD4+ T cell priming and Th2/Th17 responses.

Plasmacytoid dendritic cell (pDC).description: Specialized IFN-producing cells that sense viral nucleic acids through TLR7/9 and bridge innate and adaptive immunity.

Monocyte-derived dendritic cell (DC3).description: Inflammatory dendritic cells derived from monocytes, sharing features with macrophages and DCs, often expanded in inflammation.

Alveolar macrophage.description: Tissue-resident macrophages of the alveolar space involved in surfactant metabolism and immune surveillance.

Classical monocyte.description: Blood-derived monocyte precursors that enter tissues and can differentiate into macrophages or dendritic cells.

Alveolar Macrophage.description: Resident macrophages lining the alveolar spaces, specialized in surfactant lipid metabolism and homeostatic immune surveillance.

Interstitial Macrophage.description: Tissue-resident macrophages located in the lung interstitium, often perivascular, involved in immunoregulation and tissue remodelling.

Monocyte-derived Macrophage.description: Recently recruited macrophages that differentiate from blood monocytes in response to inflammation, exhibiting pro-inflammatory functions.

SPP1+ Lipid-associated Macrophage.description: A profibrotic macrophage population associated with lipid accumulation and chronic lung disease, marked by SPP1 and extracellular matrix components.

Dendritic Cell (cDC2).description: Conventional type 2 dendritic cells specialized in antigen presentation and T cell activation, distinguished by CD1c and FCER1A expression.

Classical Monocyte.description: Circulating blood monocytes that infiltrate tissues upon inflammation, expressing high CD14 and FCN1.

Neutrophil.description: Granulocytic innate immune cells with potent antimicrobial functions, characterized by azurophilic granule proteins.

Lymphatic capillary endothelial cell.description: Initial lymphatic endothelial cells lining blind-ended capillaries that absorb interstitial fluid and immune cells in the lung parenchyma.

Collecting lymphatic endothelial cell.description: Lymphatic endothelial cells forming larger collecting vessels with valves and smooth muscle coverage, actively transporting lymph in the lung parenchyma.

Blood vascular endothelial cell.description: Endothelial cells lining blood vessels in the lung, including arteries, veins, and capillaries, distinct from lymphatic vessels by lacking typical lymphatic markers.

Alveolar Type I Cell.description: Thin squamous cells lining the alveolar surface, specialized for gas exchange and barrier function.

Alveolar Type II Cell.description: Cuboidal surfactant-producing cells that serve as progenitors for alveolar epithelium during repair.

Club Cell.description: Secretory cells of the bronchiolar epithelium with detoxifying and immunomodulatory functions.

Ciliated Cell.description: Motile multiciliated cells that propel mucus and debris upwards along the bronchiolar surface.

Alveolar Macrophage.description: Resident immune cells of the alveolar space, responsible for surfactant clearance and host defense.

Pulmonary Fibroblast.description: Mesenchymal cells of the lung interstitium that produce extracellular matrix and support alveolar structure.

Alveolar fibroblast.description: Fibroblasts located in the alveolar interstitium, maintaining alveolar structure and surfactant homeostasis.

Adventitial fibroblast.description: Fibroblasts located in the perivascular and peribronchial adventitia, contributing to extracellular matrix production.

Myofibroblast.description: Activated contractile fibroblasts expressing smooth muscle actin, important in wound healing and fibrosis.

Lipofibroblast.description: Lipid-droplet-containing fibroblasts in the alveolar niche, supporting alveolar type 2 cells and surfactant production.

Smooth muscle cell.description: Contractile cells of the airway and vascular smooth muscle, expressing contractile proteins.

Pericyte.description: Perivascular cells wrapped around capillaries, regulating blood flow and vessel stability.

Mesothelial cell.description: Epithelial cells lining the pleural cavity, with microvilli and secretory functions.

Hematopoietic stem cell.description: Pluripotent hematopoietic stem cell capable of self-renewal and differentiation into all blood cell lineages; rare in lung parenchyma unless in circulation.

Monocyte.description: Migratory myeloid cell that can differentiate into macrophages or dendritic cells; commonly found in blood and lung interstitium; often confused with hematopoietic stem cells due to shared myeloid progenitor markers.

Endothelial cell.description: Cell lining blood vessels and capillaries, highly abundant in lung; expresses CD34 and other stem-associated markers, leading to potential confusion with hematopoietic stem cells.

Alveolar macrophage.description: Tissue-resident macrophage of the alveolar space, involved in surfactant clearance and immune surveillance; expresses some myeloid progenitor genes and may be confused with hematopoietic stem cells in lung parenchyma.

Pulmonary ionocyte.description: Rare FOXI1+ epithelial cell specialized in ion transport, highly expressing CFTR and located primarily in conducting airways.

Pulmonary neuroendocrine cell.description: Airway epithelial cells with neuroendocrine function, secreting neuropeptides and chromogranins in response to stimuli.

Tuft cell.description: Chemosensory epithelial cell expressing taste-related genes and POU2F3, involved in immune signaling and mucosal responses.

Alveolar Macrophage.description: Resident macrophages of the alveolar lumen specialized in surfactant turnover and lipid metabolism, expressing PPARG, FABP4, MARCO, and high levels of CHIT1 and CCL18.

Interstitial Macrophage.description: Tissue-resident macrophages located in the lung interstitium, often perivascular, characterized by high expression of CD14, LYVE1, FOLR2, and MERTK, with a role in tissue remodeling and immune surveillance.

Monocyte-derived Macrophage.description: Inflammatory macrophages recently recruited from blood monocytes, expressing high FCN1, S100A8/A9, and inflammatory cytokines, and adapting to the tissue microenvironment.

Dendritic Cell.description: Antigen-presenting cells of the lung parenchyma that initiate adaptive immunity, distinguished by expression of FLT3, CLEC10A, and cDC2 markers CD1c and FCER1A.

Monocyte.description: Circulating and marginated blood monocytes that can infiltrate lung tissue, characterized by high FCN1, S100A8/A9, and low expression of tissue-resident macrophage markers.

Capillary Pericyte.description: Mural cells specific to capillaries, expressing high PDGFRB and NG2, with low contractile protein levels and roles in angiogenesis and barrier maintenance.

Arteriolar Pericyte.description: Pericyte-like cells on pre-capillary arterioles, co-expressing some smooth muscle contractile genes alongside core pericyte markers.

Vascular Smooth Muscle Cell.description: Contractile cells of larger blood vessel walls, distinguished by high MYH11 and ACTA2 expression, often confused with pericytes due to shared mural markers.

Alveolar Fibroblast.description: Fibroblasts residing in the alveolar interstitium, producing extracellular matrix components and supporting alveolar structure.

Myofibroblast.description: Activated fibroblast phenotype expressing contractile proteins and ECM, common in fibrotic regions and often confused with activated pericytes.

MCT mast cell.description: Mucosal-type mast cells expressing tryptase but lacking chymase, prevalent in lung alveolar parenchyma.

MCTC mast cell.description: Connective tissue-type mast cells co-expressing tryptase and chymase along with carboxypeptidase, found in perivascular and peribronchial lung regions.

basophil.description: Granulocytic cells that share FcεRI expression with mast cells but are distinguished by CD123 and CD13 positivity, and absence of KIT.

Resting mesothelial cell.description: Quiescent mesothelial cells lining the pleural surface, expressing characteristic epithelial and mesothelial markers, maintaining barrier function.

Activated mesothelial cell.description: Reactive mesothelial cells undergoing mesothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (MMT) in response to injury or inflammation, acquiring fibroblast-like characteristics.

Proliferating mesothelial cell.description: Dividing mesothelial cells identified by cell cycle gene expression, representing a transient regenerative population.

Fibroblast.description: Mesenchymal cells of the connective tissue, distinct from mesothelial cells by abundant extracellular matrix production and lack of epithelial markers.

Alveolar epithelial type 1 cell.description: Squamous epithelial cells covering the alveolar surface, specialized for gas exchange and characterized by expression of caveolin, aquaporin, and RAGE.

Mature goblet cell.description: Fully differentiated mucus-producing goblet cell characterized by high expression of mucin genes MUC5AC and MUC5B, and secretory markers like TFF3, CLCA1, and AGR2.

Nascent goblet cell.description: Immature goblet cell with lower mucin expression, enriched in transcription factors SPDEF and FOXA3, and early secretory markers, representing a developmental intermediate.

Intermediate secretory cell (goblet/club.description: Biphenotypic secretory cell co-expressing markers of goblet (MUC5AC) and club (SCGB1A1) cells, likely a transitional state in the airway epithelium.

Club cell.description: Non-mucous secretory cell of the airway epithelium expressing secretoglobins SCGB1A1 and SCGB3A1, and involved in detoxification and immune defense.

Ciliated cell.description: Motile ciliated cell of the airway epithelium characterized by expression of the master transcription factor FOXJ1 and structural components of cilia.

Canonical multiciliated cell.description: Typical multiciliated columnar epithelial cells with motile cilia that mediate mucociliary clearance.

Immunomodulatory multiciliated cell.description: Multiciliated cells that upregulate MHC class II molecules and antigen presentation machinery, potentially involved in immune surveillance.

Bronchiolar multiciliated cell.description: Multiciliated cells of the distal bronchioles that co-express markers typical of club cells, reflecting a hybrid phenotype.

Club cell.description: Secretory epithelial cells of the bronchioles, responsible for detoxification, immune defense, and epithelial repair.

Goblet cell.description: Mucus-secreting epithelial cells of the airway, characterized by large secretory granules and production of mucins.

Ciliated Cells Type 1.description: Multiciliated epithelial cells enriched for genes encoding dynein arm proteins, characteristic of proximal airways.

Ciliated Cells Type 2.description: Multiciliated epithelial cells enriched for radial spoke and central pair apparatus genes, found in distal bronchioles.

Secretory Club Cells.description: Non-ciliated secretory cells of the bronchiolar epithelium, expressing club cell secretory protein (CCSP) and involved in detoxification.

Goblet Cells.description: Mucus-secreting cells of the airway epithelium, characterized by expression of mucins and SPDEF transcription factor.

Basal Cells.description: Airway epithelial stem/progenitor cells, identified by TP63 and keratin expression, residing adjacent to the basement membrane.

Alveolar myofibroblast.description: Myofibroblasts residing in the alveolar interstitium, characterized by contractile proteins and production of alveolar extracellular matrix components.

Contractile myofibroblast.description: Myofibroblasts highly expressing smooth muscle contractile machinery, likely contributing to tissue tension and wound contraction.

Matrix-producing myofibroblast.description: Myofibroblasts with a secretory phenotype, abundantly producing collagens and matricellular proteins for tissue remodeling.

Fibroblast.description: Resident lung fibroblasts that maintain ECM homeostasis and do not express contractile proteins like ACTA2.

Smooth muscle cell.description: Contractile cells of the airway and vascular walls, distinguished by high MYOCD, KCNMB1, and calcium channel expression.

Pericyte.description: Perivascular cells that wrap around capillaries, crucial for vascular stability, marked by PDGFRB, RGS5, and CSPG4.

Goblet cell.description: Mucus-secreting epithelial cell of the conducting airways, characterized by high expression of MUC5AC and TFF3, playing a key role in mucociliary clearance and innate immunity.

Club cell.description: Non-ciliated secretory epithelial cell of the bronchioles, expressing SCGB1A1 and involved in detoxification and immune defense, serving as a progenitor for ciliated and goblet cells.

Serous cell.description: Secretory epithelial cell found in airway submucosal glands and surface epithelium, producing antimicrobial proteins such as lysozyme and lactoferrin.

Ciliated cell.description: Terminally differentiated epithelial cell with motile cilia, driven by FOXJ1, essential for mucociliary clearance of pathogens and debris.

Basal cell.description: Progenitor epithelial cell anchored to the basal lamina, expressing TP63 and KRT5, capable of self-renewal and differentiation into secretory and ciliated lineages.

CD56bright NK cell.description: Cytokine-producing natural killer cells with high CD56 expression and low cytotoxicity, predominantly regulating immune responses via cytokine secretion.

CD56dim NK cell.description: Mature cytotoxic natural killer cells with high CD16 expression, poised for antibody-dependent cell cytotoxicity and direct target cell killing.

Lung-resident NK cell.description: Tissue-resident natural killer cells expressing CD69, CD49a, and chemokine receptors, maintaining local homeostasis in the lung parenchyma.

ILC1.description: Type 1 innate lymphoid cells producing interferon-gamma and TNF, lacking potent cytotoxic machinery, and involved in early defense and tissue inflammation.

Cytotoxic T cell.description: CD8+ T lymphocytes recognizing peptide-MHC I complexes, mediating adaptive cellular cytotoxicity through perforin and granzymes.

NKT cell.description: T cells expressing invariant or diverse T cell receptors and NK cell markers, bridging innate and adaptive immunity by rapidly producing cytokines like IFN-γ and IL-4.

Non-classical monocytes.description: Patrolling monocytes characterized by CD16 expression and high CX3CR1, surveying vasculature and contributing to innate immunity in the lung.

Classical monocytes.description: Inflammatory monocytes expressing high CD14 without CD16, rapidly recruited to lung tissue upon infection or injury.

Intermediate monocytes.description: Pro-inflammatory monocytes expressing both CD14 and CD16, bridging classical and non-classical phenotypes and displaying antigen-presentation features.

Alveolar macrophages.description: Tissue-resident macrophages of the alveolar space involved in surfactant homeostasis and immune surveillance, often confused with monocytes due to shared myeloid markers.

Classical dendritic cells type 2 (cDC2).description: Myeloid dendritic cells specialized in antigen presentation and T cell priming, often misclassified as monocytes in parenchymal lung single-cell data.

IgA plasma cell.description: Antibody-secreting plasma cell producing IgA, important for mucosal immunity in the lung.

IgG plasma cell.description: Antibody-secreting plasma cell producing IgG, providing systemic humoral immunity.

IgM plasma cell.description: Antibody-secreting plasma cell producing IgM, often associated with primary immune responses.

Plasmablast.description: Proliferating precursor to mature plasma cells, actively secreting antibodies and expressing cell cycle genes.

B cell.description: Lymphocyte expressing surface immunoglobulin and MHC class II, capable of differentiating into antibody-secreting cells.

Plasmacytoid dendritic cell (resting).description: Resting plasmacytoid dendritic cells specialized in sensing viral nucleic acids and producing large amounts of type I interferons.

Activated plasmacytoid dendritic cell.description: Activated plasmacytoid dendritic cells with enhanced antigen-presentation capacity and strong expression of co-stimulatory molecules and interferon-stimulated genes.

Conventional dendritic cell type 2 (cDC2.description: Conventional dendritic cells type 2 specialized in antigen presentation to CD4+ T cells and expressing CD1c and CLEC10A.

Monocyte-derived dendritic cell (moDC).description: Inflammatory monocyte-derived dendritic cells that arise from circulating monocytes and express both monocytic and dendritic cell markers.

Alveolar type 1 cell.description: Squamous alveolar epithelial cells that line the majority of the alveolar surface and mediate gas exchange.

Alveolar type 2 cell.description: Cuboidal surfactant-producing alveolar epithelial cells that serve as progenitors and maintain homeostasis.

Proliferating alveolar type 2 cell.description: Alveolar type 2 cells traversing the cell cycle, essential for epithelial renewal after injury.

Transitional alveolar epithelial cell.description: Transiently appearing alveolar epithelial cells co-expressing AT2 and AT1 markers, often associated with repair processes.

Club cell.description: Secretory epithelial cells lining bronchioles, involved in host defense and xenobiotic metabolism, often found near alveolar tissue.

Ciliated cell.description: Motile ciliated cells responsible for mucociliary clearance, predominantly located in conducting airways.

Basal cell.description: Progenitor cells located in the airway basal layer, capable of differentiating into club, ciliated, and goblet cells.

Mature alveolar type 1 cell.description: Canonical squamous epithelial cells lining the alveolar surface, mediating gas exchange and fluid balance.

Alveolar type 2 cell.description: Cuboidal surfactant-producing epithelial cells of the alveoli, serving as progenitors for type 1 cells.

Alveolar type 1/2 intermediate cell.description: Transient epithelial cell state co-expressing alveolar type 1 and type 2 markers, often observed during lung regeneration and repair.

Lymphatic endothelial cell.description: Endothelial cells of the lymphatic vasculature, sharing podoplanin expression with alveolar type 1 cells but distinguishable by lymphatic-specific markers.

Alveolar fibroblast.description: Resident interstitial fibroblasts of the alveolar niche, producing extracellular matrix and occasionally mistaken for alveolar type 1 cells due to shared expression of CAV1 and other stromal genes.

Mature Alveolar Type 2 Cell.description: Terminally differentiated surfactant-producing epithelial cells lining the alveoli, essential for maintaining pulmonary surface tension and innate immunity.

Proliferating Alveolar Type 2 Cell.description: Alveolar type 2 cells in active cell cycle, responsible for self-renewal and alveolar epithelial regeneration following injury.

Transitional Alveolar Epithelial Cell (A.description: Transient differentiating alveolar epithelial cells co-expressing AT2 and AT1 markers, representing an intermediate state during AT2-to-AT1 transdifferentiation in homeostasis and repair.

Alveolar Type 1 Cell.description: Thin, squamous pneumocytes covering ~95% of the alveolar surface, specialized for gas exchange and expressing typical caveolar and tight-junction proteins.

Club Cell.description: Non-ciliated secretory epithelial cells of the distal airways (bronchioles), involved in xenobiotic metabolism and innate mucosal defense, occasionally expressing low surfactant proteins.

Pulmonary Artery Endothelial Cell (Large.description: Endothelial cells lining large elastic pulmonary arteries, exposed to high shear stress, characterized by BMP/TGF-beta and Notch pathway gene expression.

Pulmonary Artery Endothelial Cell (Small.description: Endothelial cells of small muscular pulmonary arteries and arterioles, regulating vascular tone and smooth muscle interactions via pathways such as Notch, PDGF, and angiopoietin.

Pulmonary Artery Endothelial Cell (Angio.description: Activated endothelial cells involved in angiogenesis and vessel sprouting, expressing tip/stalk cell markers and matrix remodeling genes.

Pulmonary Vein Endothelial Cell.description: Endothelial cells lining pulmonary veins, distinguished by COUP-TFII and EPHB4 expression, with prominent inflammatory adhesion molecules and chemokine production.

Pulmonary Capillary Endothelial Cell.description: Endothelial cells of alveolar capillaries specialized for gas exchange, marked by aerocyte and general capillary markers including CA4, EDNRB, and HPGD.

Solitary pulmonary neuroendocrine cell.description: Individual neuroendocrine cells scattered in the bronchiolar epithelium, secreting neuropeptides to monitor airway signals.

Neuroepithelial body neuroendocrine cell.description: Clustered neuroendocrine cells forming innervated organized bodies in the airway, serving as complex oxygen sensors.

Club cell.description: Non-ciliated secretory cells of the bronchiolar epithelium contributing to host defense and metabolism of airborne toxins.

Ciliated cell.description: Motile ciliated cells lining the airways that propel mucus and trapped particles upward via coordinated ciliary beating.

Tuft cell.description: Chemosensory epithelial cells in the airways that detect luminal stimuli and initiate type 2 immune responses via cytokine secretion.

Basal Stem/Progenitor.description: Canonical multipotent basal stem cell expressing high levels of TP63, KRT5, and KRT14.

Differentiating Basal.description: Basal cell transitioning towards a luminal secretory or ciliated phenotype with upregulation of KRT8, KRT18, and mucin-related genes.

Cycling Basal.description: Proliferating basal cell expressing cell cycle genes such as MKI67 and TOP2A.

Goblet-leaning Basal.description: Basal cell with a bias towards goblet cell differentiation, co-expressing basal and goblet markers including SPDEF and MUC5AC.

Club Cell.description: Secretory club cell of the airway expressing SCGB1A1 and involved in detoxification.

Ciliated Cell.description: Ciliated airway epithelial cell expressing FOXJ1 and motile cilia components.

Goblet Cell.description: Mucus-producing goblet cell expressing MUC5AC and SPDEF.

Alveolar Type 2 Cell.description: Surfactant-producing alveolar epithelial type 2 cell expressing SFTPC.

Pulmonary Neuroendocrine Cell.description: Rare airway neuroendocrine cell expressing CHGA and ASCL1.

Hillock basal-like.description: A subset of hillock cells retaining basal cell features including high expression of basal keratins and integrins, with proliferative capacity.

Hillock squamous-like.description: A terminally differentiated hillock subtype expressing squamous keratins, cornified envelope components, and protease inhibitors.

Hillock inflammatory-activated.description: An activated state of hillock cells characterized by upregulation of innate immune cytokines, chemokines, and stress response genes.

Basal cell.description: Classic airway basal progenitor cells expressing KRT5, KRT14, TP63, and lacking hillock-specific differentiation markers.

Secretory epithelial cell.description: Mucus-secreting secretory cells including club and goblet cells, marked by SCGB1A1, MUC5B, and other secretory products.

Squamous metaplastic cell.description: Squamous epithelial cells arising from metaplasia, expressing terminal differentiation markers like KRT10, FLG, and LOR.

Airway smooth muscle cell.description: Contractile cells surrounding bronchi and bronchioles that regulate airway tone and express hedgehog pathway components.

Arterial smooth muscle cell.description: Smooth muscle cells lining pulmonary arteries, characterized by high Notch signaling and arterial-specific markers.

Venous smooth muscle cell.description: Smooth muscle cells located in pulmonary vein walls, expressing venous identity markers and participating in venous capacitance.

Pericyte.description: Microvascular mural cells embedded in the capillary basement membrane, critical for vascular stability and angiogenesis.

Myofibroblast.description: Contractile interstitial cells with high extracellular matrix production, found in alveolar septa and enriched during lung repair.

Fibroblast.description: Resident mesenchymal cells producing extracellular matrix components, crucial for lung structure.

Myofibroblast.description: Contractile fibroblasts expressing alpha-smooth muscle actin, involved in wound healing and fibrosis.

Pericyte.description: Perivascular cells wrapping around capillaries, regulating vascular stability and permeability.

Vascular Smooth Muscle Cell.description: Contractile cells of the vessel wall, regulating vascular tone and blood flow.

Mesothelial Cell.description: Cells forming the pleural lining, secreting lubricant to reduce friction during respiration.

Endothelial Cell.description: Cells lining blood vessels, commonly confused with stromal cells due to shared mesenchymal markers in some contexts.

Epithelial Cell.description: Parenchymal cells of the airway and alveolar epithelium, often misclassified as stromal in undifferentiated states.

CD4+ T cell.description: Helper T cells expressing CD4 that coordinate adaptive immune responses through cytokine secretion and interaction with antigen-presenting cells.

CD8+ T cell.description: Cytotoxic T cells expressing CD8 that directly kill infected or malignant cells via granzyme and perforin release.

Regulatory T cell.description: Suppressive T cells expressing FOXP3 that maintain immune tolerance and prevent autoimmunity.

Gamma-delta T cell.description: Unconventional T cells expressing gamma-delta TCR that recognize non-peptide antigens and bridge innate and adaptive immunity.

MAIT cell.description: Mucosal-associated invariant T cells that recognize microbial vitamin B metabolites presented by MR1 and contribute to mucosal immunity.

Natural killer cell.description: Innate lymphoid cells lacking CD3 that mediate cytotoxic killing and cytokine production without antigen-specific receptors.

Innate lymphoid cell.description: An innate counterpart of T cells lacking rearranged antigen receptors, involved in tissue homeostasis and early immune responses.

MUC5AC+ Goblet Cell.description: Goblet cell subtype producing MUC5AC mucin, predominant in proximal airways and upregulated in chronic respiratory diseases.

MUC5B+ Goblet Cell.description: Goblet cell subtype producing MUC5B mucin, found throughout the airway surface epithelium and essential for normal mucus clearance.

Club Cell.description: Non-ciliated bronchiolar exocrine cell that secretes club cell secretory protein, the primary secretory cell in distal airways, often confused with goblet cells in lung parenchyma.

Ciliated Cell.description: Motile ciliated cell responsible for mucociliary clearance, frequently found adjacent to secretory cells in the tracheobronchial epithelium.

Tracheobronchial smooth muscle cell.description: Contractile smooth muscle cells of the trachea and bronchi, expressing high levels of canonical smooth muscle markers involved in airway tone regulation.

Vascular smooth muscle cell.description: Smooth muscle cells lining pulmonary blood vessels, with a transcriptional profile emphasizing vascular development genes.

Myofibroblast.description: Activated fibroblasts with contractile properties often found in fibrotic lung tissue, co-expressing alpha-smooth muscle actin and extracellular matrix components.

Pericyte.description: Mural cells surrounding capillary endothelium, characterized by expression of PDGFRB and NG2, regulating vascular stability and permeability.

Pulmonary vein endothelial cell.description: Endothelial cells lining the large pulmonary veins that carry oxygenated blood from the lung capillaries to the left atrium.

Post-capillary venule endothelial cell.description: Endothelial cells of small venules involved in leukocyte trafficking and immune surveillance.

Arterial endothelial cell.description: Endothelial cells lining pulmonary arteries, characterized by Notch signaling and high expression of arterial markers.

Alveolar capillary endothelial cell.description: Endothelial cells forming the thin gas-exchange barrier in the alveolar septa.
